# Independent audit of the prescribed-direction simplex roof capacity

The object audited is Section 6 of
`candidate 5e5b642b770e6623`.
Its universal bound and the underlying affine-overlap formula have
already received separate root and Slab audits. This audit concerns the
additional sharp optimization with the actual direction held fixed.


It supplies no mixed-integer center selection.

## Parameters and the overlap substitution

Let d>=2, beta>1, sigma>=1 and V=|T|. The source's independent
overlap formula is

    W(lambda)=V (lambda-1)/(lambda-sigma)
                    (1-sigma beta/lambda)^d, lambda>sigma beta.

Put u=1-sigma beta/lambda. Direct substitution gives

    W(lambda)/V
      =u^d [sigma beta-1+u]/[sigma(beta-1+u)]
      =u^d/sigma + ((sigma-1)/sigma) beta u^d/(beta-1+u)
      =g(u).

In particular g(0)=g'(0)=0 and g(1)=1. With a=beta-1>0,

    (u^d/(a+u))''
      =u^(d-2) [d(d-1)a^2+2d(d-2)au+(d-1)(d-2)u^2]
                    /(a+u)^3.

Every term is nonnegative and the first is positive for 0<u<1.
Thus g''>0, also when sigma=1 because its first summand suffices.
The function G(u)=g(u)+(1-u)g'(u) is continuous on [0,1],
has G(0)=0, G(1)=1, and G'(u)=(1-u)g''(u)>0 in (0,1).
Consequently every 0<b<V has one and only one optimizing u in (0,1).
The value b=V corresponds only to u=1.

## Differentiation is justified by a finite dominating measure

On the transverse projection of T, let ell be its chord length and
r=(h+U)/ell wherever ell>0. The already proved overlap identity is

    Phi(lambda)=integral (lambda-r)_+ ell dnu=lambda Vg(u).

The difference quotients of (lambda-r)_+ ell are bounded by ell,
whose integral is V. Dominated convergence gives the left and right
derivatives as the ell-weighted measures of r<lambda and r<=lambda.
The explicit expression is differentiable for lambda>sigma beta;
therefore the equality level r=lambda has zero ell-weighted measure.
Since lambda u'=1-u,

    Phi'=V[g+(1-u)g']=VG(u),
    lambda Phi'-Phi=V sigma beta g'(u).

The partial-column dual inequality applies to every convex subbody,
without an existence assumption about an optimizer. At VG(u)=b it
therefore proves the claimed lower bound for all such bodies.

## The optimizer is an actual convex body

The overlap T intersect F_lambda(T) is a full-dimensional compact
simplex in this range. Its transverse projection E_lambda is compact,
convex and full dimensional in the transverse space. Thus

    B_lambda=T intersect pi_e^(-1)(E_lambda)

is compact and convex, and it contains the full-dimensional overlap;
in particular it is a convex body. A positive-length column belongs
to E_lambda exactly when its overlap interval is nonempty, that is,
ell-(h+U)/lambda>=0 or r<=lambda. This equivalence uses the fact
that the affine image shifts each chord downward and h+L>0.
Zero-length columns have zero d-volume and zero transverse measure.
The equality-level argument above handles zero-length overlap intervals
on otherwise positive columns.

This B_lambda therefore takes full T chords exactly on the selected
ratio sublevel. Its volume is Phi'=b, and its upper endpoint there is
the original U. Its roof integral is lambda Phi'-Phi, so it attains
the claimed lower bound. No relaxation-to-convexity gap remains.

## Full-volume endpoint

For b=V use B=T. The nonnegative integrands

    min(lambda ell,h+U)

increase pointwise to h+U on the projection interior. This quantity
is bounded there, the projection is bounded, and its boundary is null.
Monotone convergence and the exact finite expansion of W yield

    R_e(T,h)=V[d sigma beta-(sigma-1)]
            =V sigma beta g'(1).

This verifies the full-volume endpoint without a finite optimizing
lambda. The claim of directional sharpness is for each single fixed
e only; no simultaneous attainment in several different directions
has been assumed.
